text:
tom: Heads-up: new Next.js starter with LangChain bindings is flaking for first-time devs. Repro steps + minimal logs below — looks like a browser vs server SDK parity/auth path issue + CORS causing retries. anyone on this?
riley: ugh, saw a couple reports. Which starter variant? `next-starter-langchain-lite`?
tom: yep that one. Steps:
1) npx create-redwood-app --template next-starter-langchain-lite
2) cd app && yarn && cp .env.local.example .env.local
3) .env.local contains: `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_abc` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_URL=https://api.redwood.example`
4) Start dev, open /playground, click "Embed text" -> browser console shows: `POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings 401` then the client SDK retries twice and throws `AuthError: invalid_token` while the server-side route that mints ephemeral tokens logs success.

anit: quick guess: the starter has a server route that mints ephemeral tokens but the client layer in the template is still using the old `@redwood/sdk-js/browser` path which expects a static key. That mismatch triggers retry/backoff code in the browser SDK that wasn't coded to fall back to the ephemeral flow.
riley: that matches. We recently shipped ephemeral token helper on server-side but didn't update the client sample code in a few older templates. The correct client should call `/api/auth/ephemeral` then attach `Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>` to requests.
tom: minimal server console snippet: `ephemeral token issued for session=dev:1, expires_in=60s` but the browser request went straight to /v1/embeddings w/out token. So it's a template wiring issue.
ci-bot: ci-bot: opening a smoke test ticket: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/issues/221 - will run dev server and simulate first-run user flow.
riley: I'll push a tiny starter patch that replaces the client-side direct SDK call with the ephemeral token flow + a tiny retry-with-refresh helper. Will also bump `@redwood/sdk-js` to include the browser parity patch.
anit: for quick devs, add a note in README: "If embedding requests 401 on first run, refresh the page after the server prints 'ephemeral token issued' or run `curl -X POST /api/auth/ephemeral` to pre-warm."
docs-bot: docs-bot: created docs PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/210 updating starter onboarding and adding ephemeral auth snippet.
tom: thanks — one more edge: the starter served via Vite HMR was prefetching the embed route on hover, so sometimes the ephemeral endpoint hadn't executed yet and the preflight triggered a CORS preflight -> 401. Suggest adding `credentials: 'include'` on the fetch and explicit `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` in the dev server express proxy.
riley: noted, adding credentials header and a tiny comment in the starter code.
ci-bot: ci-bot: smoke test updated to hit /api/auth/ephemeral before exercising embedding flow.
tom: great, once the patch lands i'll test and close the sample issue. thanks all :rocket:
